subject: City Council Candidate Paul Donato Jr
overview: Host John Petrella interviewed City Council candidate Paul Donato Jr. regarding his platform on zoning, infrastructure, and economic development. Donato emphasized focusing commercial growth on Mystic Avenue and implementing an aggressive, utility-funded road repair schedule.

items.title: Candidate Background and Motivation
items.summary: Lifelong resident Paul Donato Jr. discussed his background in the hospitality industry and his desire to represent Medford citizens who feel unheard by local government.

items.title: Zoning and Neighborhood Preservation
items.summary: The candidate advocated for concentrating high-density, mixed-use development on Mystic Avenue to protect the character and sunlight access of established residential neighborhoods.

items.title: Infrastructure and Utility Coordination
items.summary: Donato proposed a ten-year plan to overhaul 30 to 40 streets annually, requiring utility companies to fund underground repairs and curb-to-curb repaving.

items.title: Economic Development and Commercial Growth
items.summary: The discussion focused on revitalizing stagnant industrial sites like the former Cain's factory and criticized recent zoning changes enacted by the current council.

items.title: Local Business and Recreational Vision
items.summary: Donato expressed support for local "mom and pop" businesses in city squares and suggested attracting family-oriented developments like indoor water parks to the city.

items.title: Public Safety and Walkability
items.summary: The candidate addressed the poor condition of city sidewalks and the necessity of meeting ADA requirements while managing the city's tree canopy.
